Under a 10-experiment budget, it is best to start with a high-potential configuration that is also representative of a key hypothesis about multimodal synergy.

Current evidence is very sparse: only one multimodal multiprofile configuration has been tested, and it uses scgpt + imagenet_vit_l with transformer + weighted fusion. The key uncertainty is whether the strong result is driven more by the RNA encoder, the image encoder, or the fusion/aggregation choice. This experiment keeps the likely strong multimodal multiprofile setup but switches the RNA encoder to pca_n2000 while keeping the same image encoder, aggregation, and weighted fusion, directly testing whether the current gain depends on scgpt or whether a simpler RNA representation can match or improve it. Given the limited budget, this is the best next step because it most efficiently probes a high-impact design choice while staying close to the best observed configuration instead of spending a trial on a more distant or lower-priority setting.

The key uncertainty is whether the strong pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l pairing can be improved by changing only the aggregation/fusion design without changing the proven core modalities. config_004 directly tests that by swapping avgpool for transformer while keeping the same RNA/image encoders and weighted fusion, making it a clean follow-up that isolates a high-impact architectural choice. This is the best use of the next experiment because it exploits the best-performing direction so far while still probing a likely source of additional gain.

This experiment tests whether the same strong backbone benefits from a different aggregation choice under the best observed fusion scheme, specifically isolating whether avgpool is truly better than transformer with scgpt-free, high-performing settings. It is the best next use of budget because it directly probes the most promising configuration neighborhood, is grounded in the strongest result so far, and can either confirm the current lead or reveal an even better variant without wasting the remaining budget on clearly less promising model families.

The strongest evidence so far is that multimodal with imagenet_vit_l and pca_n2000 + weighted fusion is best, while scgpt underperformed in the same general setup. However, we have not yet tested whether scgpt can recover performance when paired with the stronger multimodal transformer+concat design that often helps more expressive fusion. This experiment tests that key interaction: a higher-capacity fusion/aggregation choice with the currently unproven scgpt+imagenet_vit_l multimodal combination. Given the limited remaining budget, it is the best next step because it directly probes a plausible high-ceiling extension of the current best-performing family while reducing uncertainty about whether the poor scgpt results were due to the encoder itself or the fusion/aggregation choice.

The strongest evidence so far is that multimodal + multiprofile with pca_n2000 and imagenet_vit_l is promising, especially the avgpool + weighted result (0.635 acc), but we have not yet isolated whether the gain comes from avgpool or from the fusion choice. This experiment tests the logical extension of that best-performing family by keeping the strong encoders and switching to transformer aggregation with concat fusion, which directly clarifies whether a richer fusion/aggregation can beat the current best. Current evidence strongly favors pca_n2000 over scgpt with imagenet_vit_l in multiprofile multimodal models: pca+imagenet+avgpool+weighted is best so far (0.6352 acc), and pca+imagenet+avgpool+concat is also strong (0.6287), while scgpt variants are much worse. What remains uncertain is whether a transformer aggregator can improve over avgpool when paired with the promising pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l backbone, and whether concat fusion can preserve the gains seen with pca. This test directly probes that high-potential extension of the best-performing direction, making it the best use of a remaining experiment under a limited budget.
